newsitem.title: USA: NYS low debt ratings carry high cost - comptroller.
newsitem.headline: NYS low debt ratings carry high cost - comptroller.

text.p: New York State's poor credit rating is costing taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars, according to a report issued on Wednesday by state Comptroller H. Carl McCall.
Two of the major rating agencies -- Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp -- both rate New York's debt lower than that of most other states, McCall said in a statement.
S&P rates New York State's debt A-minus, which is also the rating on Louisiana's debt, the lowest in the nation, McCall said.
Moody's rates the state's debt A2.

According to McCall's estimate, if the state's rating was just one notch higher, it would have save $158 million in interest costs over the life of the $6.9 billion of debt issued between January 1, 1995, and August 31, 1996, the time period examined in his report.
McCall also said late budgets contribute to the state's rating problems.

"Late budgets are just not an inconvenience or aggravation -- they're expensive," he said. "Rating agencies have made it clear an important step New York could take to improve its credit rating is to pass a budget on time.

"But here we are again, 85 days late, inching toward another record," McCall said. "If New York demonstrated responsible budget practices strong enough to merit an upgrade, the state could save taxpayers $10 million a year in debt service."
"Poor budgeting means low credit ratings, and low credit ratings mean higher borrowing costs -- it's that simple," McCall said. ((--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650))
